newsitem.title: FRANCE: Major rescue exercise planned in Channel Tunnel.
newsitem.headline: Major rescue exercise planned in Channel Tunnel.

text.p: The Channel Tunnel's emergency services will stage major rescue practices on Sunday, evacuating passsengers from an Eurostar high-speed train and a train shuttle, sources at operator Eurotunnel said on Saturday.

The sources said the tunnel's safety commission had requested the fully-fledged evacuation exercise before deciding whether to re-open the tunnel to passengers after last week's blaze on a freight train.

A Eurostar train carrying staff of the French railway company SNCF, including chairman Louis Gallois, will leave Paris at 9 a.m. (0800 GMT) on Sunday to pick up Eurotunnel staff in Calais and Folkestone.

The simulated accident will take place on the return journey at the position of last week's fire, but in the undamaged parallel tunnel. The evacuation will be staged in the worst possible circumstances, the sources said.
The safety commission wants to check whether the third service tunnel would be sufficient to evacuate all 900 passengers from a train.
The fire, on a train carrying trucks and 34 passengers and crew, has halted passenger rail services between France and Britain. Freight traffic has resumed partially.

Eurotunnel plans to resume passenger traffic as soon as possible, shunting trains between the two tunnels to avoid the part damaged by fire. Repairs on the tunnel are expected to last three to five months.
